notes: Stored edit (0013, added for relation-property coverage, CRITERIA Rule 12) with background-belief queries. Derivability very_unlikely: 'Austin is the capital of Texas' is stated about a thousand times verbatim and follows from no other fact. Relation has_capital; the two determinate queries go through its inverse capital_of (named in `via`), which carries subproperty:located_in and the declared chain located_in->located_in. Juárez was chosen because it crosses a national border (it lies across the Rio Grande from El Paso), so both property queries discriminate: before the edit Juárez is in Chihuahua, Mexico; after it, the capital of Texas must be in Texas and so in the United States. Juárez is not a state capital itself (Chihuahua's capital is Chihuahua city), so the functional exclusion on capital_of takes nothing else away. Dropped routes: 'Juárez is in Mexico' (by name) contradicts the subproperty and the chain once Juárez is the capital of Texas; the alternative, Texas leaving the United States, contradicts firm facts outside the chain. So both are determinate; the city's side facts (in Chihuahua, its most populous city) give way with the edit. Worlds: two independent storage choices (the Legislature and the Governor's Mansion, each by name or through 'the state capital'), combined into four, as in geography-replace-0001. A rule placing a state legislature at the seat of government is real (the Texas Constitution fixes sessions at the seat of government), so the description route is one a model can hold. Near query: New Mexico's capital (Santa Fe), not the new answer. R2: no prompt names its answer; 华雷斯城 is the standard Chinese name and says nothing about Texas. Since 2026-10-31 (formal check, FINDINGS C1) every world lists the forced side fact that Juárez leaves Mexico, and the country query states its one-country presupposition as a bridge.
